title: Quasi-compact separated direct image preserves quasi-coherence on spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with these properties as defined in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. For any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], its module direct image $f_*F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ is quasi-coherent. Here $f_*$ denotes direct image for the morphism of ringed small etale topoi induced by $f$, with the scalar action from $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), restricted to separated morphisms; separated implies quasi-separated since a closed immersion is quasi-compact. Ringed direct image is spaces-properties.tex equation-push-pull preceding Tag 03LV.

proof.text: For an affine etale $V\to Y$, include it with a scheme atlas $W\to Y$ in the jointly surjective family $\{V,W\}\to Y$. The atlas exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]; [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] makes $f_V:X_V=X\times_YV\to V$ quasi-compact separated. The canonical isomorphism of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies $(f_*F)|_V$ with $(f_V)_*(F|_{X_V})$. It suffices to prove this quasi-coherent for every $V$: every object of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ has an affine open cover, and composing that cover with the covers supplying local presentations on the $V$ gives precisely the local presentations in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 03M9, first proof paragraph; properties-of-spaces Tag 03LX for restriction.

proof.text: Fix $V$ and abbreviate $X_V,f_V$ by $X,f$. Testing quasi-compactness at $\mathrm{id}_V$ gives a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $X$, by [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] to obtain a surjective etale $p:U\to X$ with $U$ affine. For this $p$ twice, [lem-trf-space-separated-affine-chart-overlap] gives the affine scheme $R=U\times_XU$ and quasi-compact separated scheme maps $a=f\circ p:U\to V$ and $b:R\to V$.

The etale restrictions $F_U$ and $F_R$ are quasi-coherent: restrict each local presentation of $F$ to the localized sites, using [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and the etale restriction description of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. The atlas equalizer [lem-trf-space-pushforward-atlas-equalizer] identifies $f_*F$ with $\ker(a_*F_U\to b_*F_R)$, where the map is the difference of the two projection restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03M9, exact sequence from Tag 03M8; properties-of-spaces Tags 03LV, 03LW for restrictions.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], write $F_U\simeq(H_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F_R\simeq(H_R)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for quasi-coherent Zariski modules. Its direct-image clause applies to the quasi-compact separated scheme maps $a,b$ of Step 2: $a_*F_U\simeq(a_*H_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $b_*F_R\simeq(b_*H_R)_{\mathrm{et}}$ are quasi-coherent on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. Their module kernel is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-etale-quasi-coherent-kernel]. Step 3 identifies that kernel with $f_*F$, and Step 1 proves the assertion on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. These are the canonical ringed module direct images, so all maps use the specified $\mathcal O_Y$ action.

source.place: Tag 03M9, final paragraph; descent Tag 03LC (3) and Tag 0GNB (3).

proof_origin.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), proof, with Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), Tag 03LX (module etale base change), Descent Tag 03LC, and Descent Tag 0GNB (3) for kernels of quasi-coherent etale modules.
